recommendation: Keep the commit as-is. It is a narrow correction to the already-applied example and prevents implementers from learning the wrong extension URL or the wrong contextInvariant evaluation focus.
issue_request: FHIR-13350 was Published/Persuasive for STU3 and requested examples for using FHIRPath with extensions, with an Address.line extension scenario as the motivating case.
initial_application: The original application was git-svn revision 13456, commit 2d851a5728d58782324e3841286fb5e9172629e4, which added the Context Invariants example and clarified StructureDefinition.contextInvariant semantics. That text persisted but mismatched the house-number example with a street-name URL and used line.exists() despite the current contextInvariant focus being the element that holds the extension.
additional_context: The current StructureDefinition source says contextInvariant expressions are evaluated only when the extension is present and with focus on the element holding the extension. The Extension Pack house-number extension is scoped to Address.line, and defining-extensions.html is an active extensibility narrative page linked from the current source.
reconciliation: Changed source/defining-extensions.html to state that the Address.line element carrying the house-number extension needs a value, changed the contextInvariant example to hasValue(), and replaced the stale implicit street-name antecedent with focus-based explanatory text.
source_changes: source/defining-extensions.html: updated the Context Invariants example for the house-number extension to use hasValue() on the Address.line element carrying the extension and removed the stale street-name implicit condition.
